commitResults.messageBody:
Rename EVException to EvException, since an abbreviation used as part of
a longer name keeps only its first letter capitalised. Rename
TaskList.asList to getTasks, because method names must be verbs, and the
Ui field `in` to `scanner`, because a field's scope is too large for a
two-letter name.

Wrap the two lines in Storage that ran past the 110-character soft
limit, and initialise skippedLineCount where it is declared.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record the coding and commit standards in AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
The standard applies to all code added from now on, so the rules that
come up most in this project are written down where both the student and
any AI assistant working in this repository will read them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a find command to search task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
A long list is hard to scan, and the list and on commands can only show
everything or one date's worth. Add `find <keyword>`, which shows the
tasks whose description contains the keyword.

The search ignores capitalisation and matches part of a word, so `boo`
finds `book`. It looks at the description only: dates are no longer
stored as text, so matching them here would be inconsistent with how
they are shown. Matching tasks keep the number they have in the full
list, as the on command already does, so a task can be marked or deleted
without listing everything first.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Three UI test cases cover a plain search, case insensitive and partial
matches, and the two ways a search can come back with nothing to show.
Seven JUnit tests cover Task.hasKeyword and Parser.parseKeyword.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-9 into master
Merge branch-A-JavaDoc into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Conflicts in Parser, Task and Ui: both branches added lines in the same
places, the find branch adding members and this branch adding the header
comments above them. Both sides are kept in each case.

The documentation branch was cut before find existed, so its members
arrived undocumented. Add header comments for Task.hasKeyword,
Parser.parseKeyword, Ui.showMatchingTasks and the FindCommand class, so
that every non-private class and method is documented as the increment
intended.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-CodingStandard into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Six files conflicted in the same way: this branch renamed the exception
class and reflowed a few lines, while master had added a header comment
directly above each signature. Keep the comments and apply the renames
to them as well, so that no @throws tag still names EVException.

EVException.java came in as a modify/delete conflict, because a rename
looks like a delete to Git and master had modified the old file. Resolve
it by keeping the rename and moving the header comments into
EvException.java.

Two changes needed redoing by hand after taking master's side of the
conflicts: TaskList.asList becomes getTasks, and the two Storage lines
that ran past the length limit stay wrapped. The find command and its
tests also still named EVException in places neither branch touched, so
Git reported no conflict there at all.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the coding standard with Checkstyle
commitResults.messageBody:
The standard was being followed by hand and by review, which is how a
duplicate import survived in ParserTest: it was added on one branch and
merged without conflict, so nothing flagged it.

Add the Checkstyle plugin with the configuration from AddressBook
Level 3, which encodes the same SE-EDU standard this project already
follows. Checking is now part of `gradlew build`, so a violation fails
the build rather than waiting to be noticed.

Fix the 24 violations found: the duplicate import, and the arrow switch
cases in Parser and Storage, which the configuration wants indented one
level from the switch itself.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-CheckStyle into master
Add a JavaFX window for the chatbot
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui used to print each reply as it worded it, which a window cannot use.
It now only records what EV says, and a caller takes the text with
takeResponse. ConsoleUi overrides that to also print the reply between
divider lines, so the terminal keeps the exact output it had, dividers,
banner and scanner included, none of which belong in a window.

EV gains getResponse, which parses one line, runs the command and hands
back what Ui collected. The terminal loop and the window now differ only
in where the text goes; the commands, task list and storage are shared.

The JavaFX classes live in ev.gui so that the text UI test runner, which
compiles with plain javac and no JavaFX on its class path, can skip that
one folder. Launcher is separate from Main because a main class that
extends Application cannot be loaded before the toolkit is running.

All 36 text UI test cases still pass unchanged, which is the point: the
window is an addition, not a replacement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-10 into master
Build EvException messages from separate lines
commitResults.messageBody:
Nineteen of the twenty-six places that raise an EvException were joining
two lines by hand, one saying what went wrong and one showing what to
type instead. The line break is now the exception's business: its
constructor takes the lines as varargs and joins them.

The structure of these messages becomes visible in the code rather than
hidden inside a concatenation, a single-line message still needs no
special case, and the separator is stated once instead of nineteen
times.

Task.encode already used varargs for the fields a subclass adds to its
save line, which is the same idea applied to a different problem.

Output is unchanged: all 36 text UI cases compare the messages verbatim
and still pass.
